children: Yuba City community leader, longtime bank director, businessman, and friend remembered for his counsel, service, and lasting contributions
YUBA CITY, Calif., Sept. 10, 2026

-- River Valley Community Bancorp (OTC Markets: RVCB), parent company of River Valley Community Bank (collectively referred to as the “Bank”), today announced with deep sadness the unexpected passing of founding and sitting director Michael C. “Mike” Wheeler, who passed away peacefully on August 29, 2026, surrounded by family. Mr. Wheeler was 76.

Mr. Wheeler was a founding member of River Valley Community Bank in 2006 and served continuously on the Board of Directors until his passing. His business judgment, steady leadership, and deep commitment to the Yuba-Sutter community helped shape the Bank’s formation, growth, and enduring focus on relationship-based community banking.

“Mike was more than a founding director of River Valley Community Bank — he was a trusted advisor, a wise counselor, and friend,” said John M. Jelavich, President and Chief Executive Officer of River Valley Community Bank. “His perspective was always thoughtful and grounded in what was best for our customers, shareholders, employees, and community. We are deeply grateful for his many years of service, and he will be greatly missed by all of us.”

“Mike’s contributions to River Valley Community Bank began at its founding and continued through years of thoughtful board service,” said Steve Danna, Board Chair of River Valley Community Bank. “He brought sound judgment and a deep understanding of our community to every discussion. We valued his counsel, his friendship, and his unwavering commitment to the Bank’s mission. His presence will be deeply missed.”

Mr. Wheeler’s service to community banking began decades before River Valley Community Bank was founded. In 1975, he was a founding member of California Independent Bancorp and Feather River State Bank, serving on the boards of both organizations through 2004 and as Chairman of Feather River State Bank from 1988 to 1993. His experience as a local business owner, community banker, and civic leader brought invaluable perspective to River Valley Community Bank’s boardroom.

Beyond his service to the Bank, Mr. Wheeler was widely respected as a longtime Yuba-Sutter business and community leader. After earning his B.A. in Economics and MBA from Stanford University, he returned to Yuba City in 1973 and dedicated more than five decades to the family automobile business, serving as General Manager, President, and Chief Executive Officer. He was also an active supporter of local youth sports, including decades of leadership, coaching, and sponsorship that helped strengthen soccer programs and facilities throughout the community.

River Valley Community Bank extends its heartfelt condolences to Mr. Wheeler’s family, friends, colleagues, and all who were fortunate to know him. His legacy of integrity, generosity, service, and friendship will remain an important part of the Bank’s history and the community he served so faithfully.
At the family’s request, memorial contributions may be made in Mr. Wheeler’s memory to the local Walk to End Alzheimer’s, a cause that held special meaning for him in honor of his father.
